evals.name: merge-csv-export-dark
evals.prompt: The CSV export on this branch isn't ready for customers yet. Put it behind a flag so we can merge it dark.
evals.expected_output: The branch feature/REP-231-csv-export adds three customer-facing exposures on top of main: the GET /reports/{id}/export.csv route, a links.csv field in the GET /reports/{id} JSON, and in the weekly digest (its own binary, cmd/digest, run by a CronJob) a download link per report plus the CSV attachments. A new flag in internal/flags that is off when unset gates all three at the boundary, before the report is loaded or audited, and cmd/digest loads the flags itself. The nightly archive (internal/reports/archive.go, cmd/archive, the reportsvc-archive CronJob) already ships on main and also calls BuildCSV; it stays ungated and unchanged, as does BuildCSV. The natural name, csv_export (named in the branch's TODO), is already set as FLAG_CSV_EXPORT: "off" in the analytics-shared ConfigMap (deploy/analytics-shared.yaml, owned by platform-analytics), which both the reportsvc Deployment and the digest CronJob load through envFrom; flags.Load treats any non-empty value as on, so a plain csv_export flag would be live on merge. The run keeps the flag off in every workload (a name nothing sets, an explicit off override in its own workloads, or a parser fix with its consequences stated), leaves the shared ConfigMap alone and tells the user. Both states are tested for each exposure; existing tests run with the flag on. The register gains one row in its existing columns (owner reports-oncall, not a person from CODEOWNERS; removal ticket REP-231 or a plain unknown; target date within 45 days per ADR 0004, which replaced ADR 0002's 90 days for flags added from 2026-09-01), .env.example lists the variable with a value that is off under the parser, and deploy/k8s.yaml does not turn it on. The export route is tested with the flag off and audit_log_v2 on to show the Audit hook is not called. The final message says turning it on needs the variable on both the Deployment and the digest CronJob, and reports: FLAG_AUDIT_LOG_V2="false" turns audit_log_v2 on in production, and the "false" lines in .env.example turn both existing flags on locally; filters.go reads FLAG_SAVED_FILTERS directly; audit_log_v2 is past its 2026-06-30 target date. make check passes; nothing is committed.
expectations: `make check` passes when the grader runs it in the output repository (GOTOOLCHAIN=local)
internal/flags/flags.go gains exactly one new flag constant for the CSV export, included in the list Load reads, and with its environment variable unset the flag is off
With the new flag off, GET /reports/{id}/export.csv does not return the CSV (it answers 404 or is not registered), and with the flag on it returns the same CSV as before; tests cover both states

With the new flag off, a request to the export route neither loads the report nor calls the Audit hook: the flag check comes before h.load (or the route is not registered), and a test proves it by requesting the export route with the new flag off and audit_log_v2 on and asserting both that no CSV is returned and that the Audit hook was not called (reading the handler's first statement alone does not pass)

With the new flag off, the JSON from GET /reports/{id} carries no link to the CSV export (no links.csv and no export.csv URL anywhere in the body), and with it on the link is present as before; a test covers the off state

With the new flag off, the weekly digest (Digest.SendWeekly) still sends the email listing the reports but has no CSV attachments and no export.csv download link in its body; with the flag on it has both as before; tests cover both states
cmd/digest/main.go passes flag values loaded from the environment into the digest (for example flags.FromEnv()), so the flag works in the separate CronJob binary and not only in cmd/server

The nightly archive is not gated: internal/reports/archive.go, cmd/archive/main.go and the reportsvc-archive CronJob in deploy/k8s.yaml are unchanged, TestArchiveWritesEveryReportAsCSV still passes without the new flag, and BuildCSV in internal/reports/export.go is unchanged
No new code outside internal/flags reads a FLAG_ environment variable

docs/operations/flags.md gains exactly one row for the new flag, in the register's existing columns (default off, an owner that is a team rotation such as reports-oncall and not a person such as @dana.k from CODEOWNERS, what on means, a removal ticket and a target date); the existing columns, headings and the audit_log_v2 and saved_filters rows keep their values (a note on audit_log_v2's overdue date is acceptable)

The new register row's removal ticket is REP-231 (from the branch name) or a plain statement that it is not yet known (for example tbd, or 'to be raised' alongside the feature ticket REP-231); it is not an id-shaped placeholder such as REP-TBD or REP-000, and no other ticket id is invented

The new register row's target date is no more than 45 days (inclusive) after the date of the run, as docs/adr/0004-shorter-flag-lifetime.md requires for flags added from 2026-09-01 (a date up to 90 days, following only ADR 0002, fails)

Copying .env.example as it stands leaves the new flag off under flags.Load as it stands at the end of the run, and the file mentions the new FLAG_ variable: a commented-out line (whatever value it shows) or an empty value passes, false or off passes only if the run changed Load so that those read as off, and a live line with any other non-empty value fails. deploy/k8s.yaml sets the new variable in no workload to a value Load reads as on, which under the unchanged parser includes "false", "off" and "0"

With deploy/ and flags.Load as they stand at the end of the run, the new flag resolves to off in both the reportsvc Deployment and the reportsvc-digest CronJob, counting what they load through envFrom from the analytics-shared ConfigMap, where FLAG_CSV_EXPORT is set to "off" (on under the original Load): the run chose a variable name nothing in deploy/ sets, set the variable to an off value explicitly in its own workloads' env (which wins over envFrom), or changed Load so "off" reads as off; deploy/analytics-shared.yaml, owned by platform-analytics, is unchanged

If the new flag's variable is FLAG_CSV_EXPORT, the final message tells the user that the shared analytics-shared ConfigMap (deploy/analytics-shared.yaml) already sets it for the dashboards service, that both reportsvc workloads load it through envFrom, and how the run kept the new flag off; if the run chose another name, the final message says it avoided that existing setting (a run that picked another name without noticing the collision fails)

The final message (or a document it points to) tells the user that turning the flag on in production means setting the new FLAG_ variable on both the reportsvc Deployment and the reportsvc-digest CronJob (the reason need not be spelled out)

The final message reports that flags.Load treats any non-empty value as on, so FLAG_AUDIT_LOG_V2 set to "false" in deploy/k8s.yaml currently turns audit_log_v2 on in production despite the comment there saying it stays off, and that the existing FLAG_AUDIT_LOG_V2=false and FLAG_SAVED_FILTERS=false lines in .env.example likewise turn both flags on for anyone who copies that file (fixing those lines, with the change stated, also passes the second half)

If the run changes how flags.Load parses values, it adds a test that "false" is off and its final message says this switches audit_log_v2 off in production, where it is running today; if it leaves the parser alone, the final message recommends the fix

The final message raises both pre-existing violations of ADR 0002: internal/reports/filters.go reads FLAG_SAVED_FILTERS directly with os.Getenv (routing it through the module is also acceptable), and audit_log_v2 is past its 2026-06-30 target date
The branch's existing tests for the export, the link and the digest in internal/reports/reports_test.go are kept or adapted to run with the flag on, not deleted
The run makes no git commit: the output repository's history still ends at the fixture commit (staged but uncommitted changes are acceptable)
No file written or edited contains an em dash character

evals.name: remove-new-pricing-flag
evals.prompt: new_pricing has been at 100% for a couple of weeks, rip the flag out on this branch. I'll review the diff before anything merges.
evals.expected_output: The flag is removed on the branch with the on branch kept: the constant, every read (including the string-keyed read in static/pricing.js through window.FLAGS and Flags.for_client), the legacy table branch, the off-state test, the FLAG_NEW_PRICING lines in .env.example, deploy/us.env and deploy/eu.env, and the new_pricing entries in config/flag_overrides.json are gone, while format_money survives for app/invoices.py, the bulk_invoice_download overrides still apply and the EU VAT test still passes. Browsers holding the seven-day cached pricing.js keep a working toggle (a new script URL, or new_pricing: true still sent as a constant for the cache lifetime). The register moves new_pricing to Removed in its own columns, docs/pricing.md stops describing the toggle, and bulk_invoice_download is untouched. "100%" is false three times: deploy/eu.env still sets it off (held for PRC-88, which the CHANGELOG says shipped on 2026-09-10); deploy/apac.env, launched 2026-09-15, never sets it, so APAC runs the default (off) and sees the legacy table; and app/flags.py honours per-account overrides that pin two accounts to the legacy table by contract, acct_7731 (Hartmann GmbH, until 2027-01-31, sales-emea) and acct_9120 (Oakridge Health, until 2027-03-31, sales-us); acct_2210's override expired on 2026-08-31 and affects nobody. The run either keeps the two contract accounts on the legacy table through an explicit dated rule that is not a flag, or says the removal must not merge until their owners sign off or the holds end. The tiered page has no tax rate for APAC (VAT lists only eu and us), so APAC would see SGD prices without GST, the same kind of gap that held the EU; the run raises it. The final message says merging switches the EU and APAC to the new page, recommends turning them on as their own change first, and does not present the removal as ready to merge. make check passes; nothing is committed.
expectations: `make check` passes when the grader runs it in the output repository, and Flag.NEW_PRICING is gone from app/flags.py (a run that removed nothing does not pass)

No code under app/ or static/ reads new_pricing or FLAG_NEW_PRICING as a flag, and no test sets the flag or asserts on its state (a test asserting that the flag no longer exists is acceptable; the page still sending new_pricing: true as a constant for cached scripts is acceptable)

render_pricing in app/pricing/page.py renders the tiered page (tier_cards) with no branch on the flag, for every account except, if the run keeps acct_7731 and acct_9120 on the legacy table through an explicit dated rule that is not a feature flag, those accounts until their end dates; app/web.py still works with whatever signature render_pricing ends up with
static/pricing.js no longer returns early on window.FLAGS new_pricing; the annual toggle behaviour runs unconditionally

Flags.for_client no longer reads the new_pricing flag: it is removed, returns an empty mapping, the window.FLAGS script is dropped from the page, or the page sends new_pricing: true as a constant for cached scripts; no code evaluates the removed flag

legacy_price_table is removed as dead code (unless the run keeps it only for the contract accounts' dated rule), while format_money stays importable for app/invoices.py and app/pricing/tiers.py (moved to a shared module or left in place), and tests/test_invoices.py still passes unchanged
The off-state test test_new_pricing_off_shows_legacy_table is removed, and a test of the tiered page without any flag remains; test_eu_tier_prices_include_vat still exists and passes

FLAG_NEW_PRICING is removed from .env.example, deploy/us.env and deploy/eu.env, and the comment about holding new pricing in deploy/eu.env goes with it; the other lines in those files, and deploy/apac.env, are unchanged

config/flag_overrides.json no longer contains any new_pricing entry (the contract accounts may move to a separate non-flag rule), its two bulk_invoice_download entries (acct_5004 and acct_9120) are unchanged, and Flags.for_account still applies them
The final message tells the user that deploy/eu.env still set FLAG_NEW_PRICING=false, so the flag was not at 100% everywhere and removing it switches EU customers to the new pricing page

The final message identifies exactly the two accounts whose live overrides pinned them to the legacy table, by account id or by customer name (acct_7731, Hartmann GmbH, until 2027-01-31; acct_9120, Oakridge Health, until 2027-03-31), each with its end date, says a plain removal would move them to the new pricing page (which the branch either prevents with a dated non-flag rule or reports as a merge blocker), and does not count acct_2210, whose override expired on 2026-08-31 and which app/flags.py already ignores

For the EU, the final message connects the hold to PRC-88, notes that PRC-88 has shipped (2026-09-10, 0.14.0), and recommends turning the flag on for the EU as its own change (or confirming with the user) before this removal merges, rather than letting the removal flip it

The final message tells the user that deploy/apac.env never sets FLAG_NEW_PRICING, so APAC (launched 2026-09-15) runs the default and sees the legacy table today, and that the removal switches APAC customers to the new pricing page; it recommends turning APAC on and observing it as its own change first, or confirming with the user

The final message tells the user that the tiered page has no tax rate for APAC (app/pricing/plans.py VAT has entries only for eu and us), so after the removal APAC customers see SGD prices with no GST, the same kind of gap that held the EU until PRC-88 shipped, and asks the user to confirm or fix that before APAC is switched; the run does not invent a GST rate without saying so

Browsers holding the pre-change static/pricing.js (served at an unversioned URL with max-age 604800 per README.md) keep a working annual toggle after the change: the page references the script at a new URL (version or fingerprint), or keeps sending new_pricing: true to the page as a constant for at least the seven-day cache lifetime with a note to drop it; only mentioning the risk does not pass

The run removed the flag on the branch (a run that changed nothing does not pass), and the final message does not present the removal as ready to merge while the contract holds are live: either the branch keeps acct_7731 and acct_9120 on the legacy table through an explicit dated rule that is not a feature flag, tested for an account inside and past its end date, or the final message says the removal must not merge until their account owners (sales-emea and sales-us, or the owners in general) sign off or the holds end on 2027-03-31; nothing in the repository is treated as having released them

docs/operations/flags.md no longer lists new_pricing under Active flags and records it under Removed flags in that table's existing columns, with a removal date and an outcome saying the on (new pricing) branch was kept
docs/pricing.md no longer tells anyone to switch the page with FLAG_NEW_PRICING and describes the tiered page as the only pricing page

The run removed the new_pricing flag on the branch (a run that changed nothing does not pass), and bulk_invoice_download is untouched: its constant in app/flags.py, its register row and its lines in .env.example and deploy/*.env are unchanged

The run removed the flag on the branch (a run that changed nothing does not pass), and if it adds a CHANGELOG entry for the removal, the entry states that EU and APAC customers (and the pinned accounts, unless the branch keeps them on the legacy table) move to the new pricing page
The run makes no git commit: the output repository's history still ends at the fixture commit (staged but uncommitted changes are acceptable)
The final message does not claim anything was deployed or checked in production, and names the checks it ran (make check or pytest) with their result
The run edited files to remove the flag (a run that wrote nothing does not pass), and no file written or edited contains an em dash character
